title: Switching failure indicator
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ sign coordinates, let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $J\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$. The switching failure indicator is $1$ if the restricted decision tree for $f$ has depth at least $k$, and is $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n$ sign coordinates
$J$ is a finite set of indices in $\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
a sign assignment is fixed on indices outside $J$
caveat: The formal statement relies on the omitted definition of restricted decision-tree depth.
